note: What has changed about one unit. A flag byte says which groups of values follow, and each group that follows says which of its values it holds and carries them as a run of bytes. The groups follow in a fixed order that is not the order of the flags: the last flag's values come before the one before it, and the rest run in flag order.

bits.name: group0
bits.note: Set where this group's values follow.

bits.name: group1
bits.note: Set where this group's values follow.

bits.note: Set where this group's values follow.

bits.name: group3
bits.note: Set where this group's values follow.

bits.name: group4
bits.note: Set where this group's values follow. They come after every other group's, whatever the flags. Nothing observed has set this, so no layout is recorded for it and a payload setting it leaves bytes unread rather than being read wrongly.

bits.name: group5
bits.note: Set where this group's values follow. They come before the group numbered after it, not after.

fields.name: unit
fields.note: The unit whose values these are.

fields.name: group0
fields.note: The values of group 0, where the flag says they follow.

fields.name: which
fields.note: Says which of the group's values the run below holds, one bit each, lowest first.

fields.name: length
fields.note: How many bytes the run below holds.

fields.name: values
fields.note: The values themselves, in the order the mask names them, lowest bit first, with nothing between them. spec/messages.md gives the shape each takes. Which of them is a number and which a measure follows from the kind of unit the identifier names, which nothing on the wire carries.
